blocks.text: SDLC 不再是一条线性的从规划到编码、测试再到部署的路径。一次代码变更、一位同事的请求，或一项生产指标，都可能触发系统中任意位置的工作。我们大多数人（以及我们的智能体）会根据手头的任务在不同阶段之间跳转。开发者把握方向、做出决策，并对最终交付的内容负责。智能体负责实施和验证变更。而一切都汇入并出自一台持续学习的机器，让下一个周期变得更好。

blocks.text: Our jobs as developers are changing. In a couple of years, we’ve gone from writing every line of code to working with AI assistants to orchestrating fleets of agents. But the goal hasn’t changed: ship completed software work. A feature, a bug fix, a security fix. Completed work, not more code, is the output that matters.

blocks.text: Today at GitHub Universe, we shared our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world. We introduced products that bring that vision to life and showed how we’re rebuilding the infrastructure underneath it.

blocks.text: Our vision: From idea to completed software

inlines.text: Our vision: From idea to completed software

blocks.text: The SDLC is no longer a linear path from planning to coding to testing to deployment. A code change, a request from a colleague, or a production metric can trigger work anywhere in the system. Most of us (and our agents) jump between different stages, depending on the task at hand. Developers set the direction, make decisions, and stay accountable for what ships. Agents implement and verify changes. And everything feeds into and out of a continuous learning machine that makes the next cycle better.

blocks.text: This agentic software delivery system solves for three things:

inlines.text: This agentic software delivery system solves for three things:
Velocity:
get from idea to completed software as quickly, efficiently, and cost-effectively as possible
Intelligence:
combine context across the platform with a continuous learning engine, so the system gets better as you use it
Quality:
make completed work secure by default and catch bugs before they ship

blocks.text: GitHub Copilot app: From issue to merge, in one app

blocks.text: The GitHub Copilot app is designed from the ground up for agentic software delivery. It connects your agents and tools across projects, so you can direct the work without making every handoff. And it’s for more than producing code: you can write specs, present design discussions, or analyze telemetry in one agent-first surface.

blocks.text: Copilot Fusion: Multi-model orchestration at its finest

inlines.text: Copilot Fusion: Multi-model orchestration at its finest

blocks.text: Different tasks need different models. Developers shouldn’t have to manage every model choice to get the right result at the right price. Copilot Fusion evaluates what a task needs across reasoning, code generation, debugging, and tool use, then chooses how to execute across one or more models. In the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, Fusion Max scored within two points of Opus 5.5 Max at half the cost and 40% less time per task.

blocks.text: Session continuity: Keep working across surfaces

inlines.text: Session continuity: Keep working across surfaces

blocks.text: Your work shouldn’t restart when you switch devices or tools. Session continuity lets you start and follow the same cloud agent session across the GitHub app, VS Code, the CLI, and the web. Start from your phone at standup, steer it from VS Code at your desk, and check in on it from github.com at lunch. The agent keeps working in the cloud. Our multi-model harness that enables it is powerful, fast, and cost-efficient.

blocks.text: Copilot automations: Learning from the results

inlines.text: Copilot automations: Learning from the results

blocks.text: Copilot automations let you create AI-powered workflows within your repo. They run in the cloud, and you can kick them off manually or set them up to respond to an event or run on a schedule. That lets you coordinate agents to handle tasks such as issue triage and code review. And now, automations can learn from their outcomes and propose improvements for you to review and approve. That’s the learning engine in practice. Use the results of the completed work to make the next run better.

blocks.text: All of this depends on a foundation that’s fast, reliable, and built to scale. Agents are changing the volume and shape of software development. Adding capacity matters, but capacity alone won’t get us there. We’ve also had to change the architecture.

blocks.text: We’re also migrating to a multi-region deployment in Azure, while continuing to serve incredible levels of traffic from developers around the world. We expect to complete the migration early next year. Those investments give us more room to grow. The next step is building the systems that handle the work.

blocks.text: We’ve scaled Git for years as activity on GitHub has grown. The agentic era calls for a different ceiling on throughput and reliability. Three principles guide our new Git architecture: simplify the primitives, decouple storage from compute, and minimize coordination.

blocks.text: Beyond the first 1%

inlines.text: Beyond the first 1%

blocks.text: Our jobs are changing, but developers are more important than ever. I think all the software we’ve written to date will amount to less than 1% of the software we’ll write in the next five years. The opportunity isn’t just to produce more code. It’s to solve problems we couldn’t solve before.
